extra.message: The attacker-controlled pageId route parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL statement passed to db.execute(), allowing UNION-based extraction or manipulation of database data.

The attacker-controlled request URL is interpolated into Jinja template source and evaluated by render_template_string(). Template expressions in a nonexistent path or query parameter are executed server-side and can invoke the globally exposed system_call helper to execute arbitrary OS commands.

cwe: CWE-1336: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements Used in a Template Engine

extra.message: Hex-decoded bytes supplied through request.form['data_obj'] are written to a file and deserialized with pickle.load(). A crafted pickle can execute arbitrary Python code during deserialization.
Base64-decoded attacker input from the URL is passed to yaml.load() under PyYAML 3.13 without a safe loader. Python-specific YAML tags can instantiate objects and execute arbitrary commands.

Untrusted XML from request.form['customers'] is parsed with xml.dom.pulldom.parseString() without disabling external entities. A crafted document can disclose local files or issue server-side requests.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: The example_file form value is used directly by open() and send_file() without constraining it to an approved directory. Absolute paths or ../ traversal sequences allow unauthenticated download of arbitrary readable files.
The search form value is rendered with Jinja autoescaping explicitly disabled. An attacker can submit HTML or JavaScript that executes in the response page.
The object returned from the attacker-controlled /about/sync pickle is rendered with autoescaping disabled. A pickle containing an HTML string therefore produces executable reflected script content.

The user-supplied link stored by /messaging/new is placed in an href without validating its URL scheme. A stored javascript: URL executes script in the application origin when a victim follows the link.
The Flask session-signing key is the hardcoded, predictable value 'random'. An attacker who knows the source can forge a session containing a truthy loggedin value and access protected content.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The privileged login credentials are hardcoded as admin/admin in runtime authentication logic, exposing a reusable administrative credential to anyone with source access.

The unauthenticated /webmaster endpoint exposes accountancy credentials and unconditionally sets session['loggedin']. Visiting it grants the session access to /confidential without presenting valid credentials.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: CORS permits every origin on every route. Flask-CORS reflects arbitrary requesting origins, and /confidential additionally sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, allowing malicious origins to read authenticated confidential responses.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Flask debug mode is enabled while the application listens on all interfaces. Unhandled route errors expose detailed stack traces and may expose the interactive Werkzeug debugger.
An active Jenkins pipeline command contains a hardcoded SonarQube authentication token in the -Dsonar.login argument. Repository readers and build-log readers can recover and reuse the credential.
